cim: St. Vincent College to launch new artificial intelligence minor
cim_eredeti: St. Vincent College to launch new artificial intelligence minor
szoveg_eredeti:
The Sis and Herman Dupré Science Pavilion is home to the Herbert W. Boyer School of Natural Sciences, Mathematics and Computing.

St. Vincent College is launching a new interdisciplinary minor in artificial intelligence.

The 18-credit minor features coursework in computer science, data science, mathematics and ethics. Students are expected to explore foundational concepts of AI, data and knowledge engineering, machine learning, and the design and implementation of AI-related technology.

The minor will emphasize both technical foundations of AI and the ethics of its use and development. The structure is flexible, allowing students to select courses across various areas of study to complement their academic interests and career goals.

The program is developed by the Computing and Information Systems and Mathematics departments, along with the Data Science program in the Herbert W. Boyer School of Natural Sciences, Mathematics and Computing.

“Artificial intelligence is a part of nearly all professions today,” said Dr. Anthony Serapiglia, chair of the Department of Computing and Information Systems. “Our goal is to provide students with a direct technical foundation and practical experience to be able to leverage what AI can do in any environment that they may find themselves in, all the while maintaining the emphasis on human responsibility and ethical considerations that are inherent in everything we do here at St. Vincent.”

Dr. Mary Regina Boland, C’10, an assistant professor of data science, said Boyer School officials recently surveyed regional employers to uncover their needs. One of the key findings was a desire for more AI training.

“This new minor in artificial intelligence will be perfect for students seeking employment in our region,” Boland said. “It can be paired nicely with several existing SVC majors, including computer science, data science, mathematics, cybersecurity and information systems.”

The program aims to equip students to take leadership roles, according to a SVC release.

“Artificial intelligence has its roots in computer science, but its applications now extend across virtually every field of study and profession,” said Dr. Stephen Jodis, Boyer School dean. “By bringing together faculty from computer science, data science, mathematics and related disciplines, we have developed a minor that gives students a strong technical foundation in AI that complements their primary areas of study. Our goal is to prepare students to understand, develop and responsibly apply these technologies in their chosen fields.”
